title: Implicit chemosensory threat signals as stimulators of amygdala hyperresponsiveness in AMD
summary: This study investigates how the smell of people in aggressive situations – for example, after provocation during boxing – affects others, especially people with mental disorders who tend to show aggressive behavior. The researchers want to find out whether such odors are subconsciously perceived as warning signals in threatening situations and thus lead to increased activation in certain brain regions. In addition, it will be examined whether previous adverse experiences in childhood influence these reactions. For this purpose, an experiment using virtual reality and brain scans will be conducted. The aim is to understand how odor, threat, and aggression are related.
conditions: All psychiatric disorders, with exceptions according to the following criteria: dementia (all forms, e.g. F00–F03), severe intellectual disability (IQ < 50), diseases involving the central nervous system (e.g. encephalitis, tumors, epilepsy, fetal alcohol syndrome), chronic physical illnesses with central neural or hormonal involvement (e.g. severe somatic or neurological diseases), acute or chronic illnesses that make it impossible to carry out the study protocol (e.g. chronic nasal diseases, lung diseases, etc.), BMI outside the normal range (<18.5 or >25) (for olfactory reasons), anosmia (complete loss of sense of smell).

interventions.name: The observational group consists of participants from the Q01 subproject of TRR 379 ("Service Project: Recruitment and biotyping transdiagnostic risk mechanisms for aggressive behaviors in mental disorders across the life span", EK 24-270), who have agreed to be contacted for participation in furthe

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Odor donors: Male, Between 18 - 55 years old, Caucasian (white), German speaking, Healthy non-smokers without medication or drug use. Donors are asked to refrain from activities that could affect their body odor (e.g. spicy food, alcohol, garlic and asparagus) for 2 days prior to donation.
Odor recipients: 18 - 40 years of age
Exclusion criteria:
Odor donors (behavioral study): Regular medication or drug use, metabolic diseases (e.g. diabetes mellitus, thyroid dysfunction, hormonal disorders), psychology students or people with increased understanding of psychological tasks and tests, smokers, diagnosed psychiatric diseases, neurological diseases
Odor recipients (MRI study): dementia, severe mental retardation (IQ < 50), insufficient ability to read and write German, inability to follow the study protocol, severe somatic or neurological diseases affecting the central nervous system or hormonal functions (such as encephalitis, brain and hormone-secreting tumors, dementia, epilepsy, fetal alcohol syndrome). Contraindications for MRI examinations, BMI below (<18.5) and above (>25) the normal range, as being underweight or overweight is associated with poorer olfactory sensitivity, frequent nosebleeds or nosebleeds within the last 3 days, chronic nasal diseases, respiratory diseases, chronic sinusitis, anosmia, lung diseases, diseases with CNS involvement, smoking, head injuries, head surgery, metabolic diseases (diabetes, thyroid), other diseases (such as hepatitis, renal insufficiency, gastrointestinal ulcers), as well as the usual MRI exclusion criteria (metal implants, pacemaker, claustrophobia). For healthy controls, additional current and previous psychiatric illnesses, drug abuse or regular use of medication
